rationale: The Old English plural "Galleas" most naturally refers to the region of Gaul (ancient western Europe) as a geographical/territorial designation, consistent with the Bede attestation (Bd. 5, 11) where it is used as a place name rather than an ethnic label. While it could also denote the Gauls as a people (gaul.n.02), the noun form "Galleas" in Bede typically references the territory, making gaul.n.03 the best fit.
